/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 67-year-old woman with a recently found hepatic carcinoma has been an inpatient for more than a week. During morning rounds, she was abnormally disoriented to time and place along with a shortened attention span. The overnight resident reports that she was coming in and out of this state for the past couple nights. The patient was known to drink often, but reported that she has not consumed alcohol in weeks leading up to her admission. She is not jaundiced and has no metabolic imbalance upon laboratory tests. What is the most likely cause of her recent mental impairment?

Options:
A. Delirium
B. Substance abuse
C. Brain metastasis
D. Delirium tremens
E. Dementia

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question asks about the etiology of acute confusional state (delirium), which is a mental disorder topic within the scope of psychiatry and mental health."}
